Synopsis:
Rath is a human druid opposed to Kagha, who has taken control of the grove in Halsin's absence. He is a kind, determined man, who seeks to keep nature in balance and prevent violence at all costs.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_ShadowDruid_Opposed.json: The party is in the goblin camp’s wolf pens, where goblin children — egged on by adults — have been tormenting a trapped bear (the archdruid Halsin is in beast form here, though he won’t disclose that). Rath, a human druid who opposes Kagha’s takeover of the Grove, is distraught at the cruelty and is pleading for mercy, invoking Silvanus and urging nonviolence. The player’s line blaming the child for stealing sets up a moral clash between retributive punishment and Rath’s insistence on protecting nature and preventing bloodshed. Off‑screen events in this cluster (stones thrown at the bear, possible combat or the bear’s retaliation) explain the tension and Rath’s emotional reaction.
- DEN_ShadowDruid_AD_LeaderPersuaded.json: Plays ONLY if Rath died in the combat against the Shadow Druids! If Rath is alive, He and Kagha have an AD together instead. In all cases, Kagha is mourning, shocked and repentant at what she has done.
- DEN_ShadowDruid_SnakesCourt.json: Druids hold court to determine whether or not to lock up a tiefling child for stealing their precious artifact. If you fail to stop them, the child tries to run and is attacked by their guardian snakes.Sagha the druid leader is the main player in this scene. She is machiavellian, and flips to evil should the snakes attack the child.
- DEN_ShadowDruid_Leader.json: Player speaks with Kagha, the secret Shadow druid. Various paths of conversation reflect whether Kagha's actions led to a child's death or not. She may be neutral/Machiavellian or pure evil, depending.
- DEN_ShadowDruid_Denouncing.json: You have confronted Kagha about being a Shadow Druid. This has initiated the transformation of the rats into shadow druids before your very eyes. The shadow druids welcome the circle into their fold; you have to fight, or convince Kagha to come around, which will be very hard - and even harder if the kid died before. Olodan the shadow druid is their leader; slobbering and sleazy.

context: The party is standing in the goblin camp’s wolf pens where goblin children, egged on by adults, have been tormenting a trapped bear (the archdruid Halsin is currently in beast form here but won’t reveal it). Rath is a compassionate human druid who opposes Kagha’s takeover of the Grove in Halsin’s absence and is desperate to prevent further cruelty or bloodshed; his repeated pleas to Silvanus come from that stance. The player line blaming the child for stealing sets up a moral clash between retributive punishment and Rath’s insistence on mercy and protecting nature. Off‑screen actions (stones thrown at the bear, possible combat or the bear’s retaliation) have already raised the tension and will shape how this incident affects later confrontations with Kagha and the druids.
